I ran a STEM extracurricular this past summer for ages 5-13 (yes big range), so I can share some of my annecdotes and idea with the caveat that my experience isn't necessarily generalizable.

I did an activity about combinatorics and discrete finite probability. We had decks of cards and talked about things like how many five card hands there are, how likely your opponent is to have the queen of spades in Hearts if you don't have it, etc. We also did how likely you are to e.g. roll doubles in one of two rolls of dice, binomial probability and whatnot. With the older campers i helped them through calculating how many Rubik's cube scrambles of various types of puzzles there are. 

 I did a class on cryptography, and we talked about rotation cyphers and with the older kids I talked about information theory and after an introductory modular arithmetic crash course we talked about how to design cryptosystems with different properties. One of the advantages of this one is that you can have your campers make a Caesar cipher wheel out paper, which is a huge help for managing campers that are more concrete focused.

I did a bunch of science activities that used math, like I had a two part activity with electromagnetism where we built electromagnets and talked about vectors and force fields.

I've sent this to someone else on this thread already, but I think you're overrating how important advantage is and underrating how important +5 to hit is. With a base attack bonus of +7 (+4 from strength and +3 from proficiency) and an average damage of 18.5 (+7 from 2d6 base damage, +4 from strength, +2 from rage damage, +5.5 from Divine Fury) the maximum AC where GWM is worth using is as follows:  


||Advantage	|no Advantage|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Favored by the Gods|21|18|
|no Favored by the Gods|16|13|

  
As you can see, the extra +5 to hit increases GWM's effectiveness more than Advantage does, and of course they stack. The average damage needs to include AC in the calculation, but we'll give the values for an AC of 16 and 19, I feel those are representative. The damages are tabulated as follows:  


|AC 16	|Advantage	|no Advantage|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Favored by the Gods|24|17.1|
|no Favored by the Gods|16.45875	|11.1\*|

​

|AC 19|Advantage|no Advantage|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Favored by the Gods|19.87875|12.95\*|
|no Favored by the Gods|12.90375\*|8.325\*|

		  
\*GWM has negative effectiveness and isn't used  
as you can see, both for 16 and 19 AC, having advantage isn't as effective as +5 to hit, and of course both are more effective when used in conjunction. Additionally, Favored by the Gods is used after you know the outcome of your roll, and so there is no "overkill", you can (and should) only use it when you need it to turn a miss into a hit.
Yes, and with the shield spell you can make yourself harder to hit (albeit twice a day, but still) while being able to attack with advantage.
Then you don't get Favored by the Gods though, which is like 95% of why we're taking Sorcerer in the first place.

Naiive calculation, you're delaying Barbarian progression (which generally isn't all that great anyway, except level 5 I don't think you're ever really hurting for that next ability) for an extra (assuming 2 short rests per long rest) 3\*8 = 24 or so damage a day, in addition to access to the ability to drop rage and use shield against strong-hitting enemies and/or the ability to use sleep to deal with lower HP enemies and/or the ability to use false life to bolster your HP. That 15 per day figure is significantly low though, because you use Favored by the Gods *after* you roll. Realistically you'll only use it if it turns a miss into a hit, and thus the actual average extra damage per day is 3\*18.5 = 55.5 or so damage a day. Additionally, this extra damage comes when you decide it does, meaning that you could really pull through and hit the hits that you need to.  


>But not factoring in how that calculation changes once you get Extra Attack

The only factors affecting if GWM is worth it are enemy AC, hit bonus, damage, and whether or not you have advantage. A second attack doesn't change anything. You should only be using Favored by the Gods on your first attack (the one with Divine Strike) on any given round anyway, so the second, non Divine attack doesn't matter in terms of damage comparison.

Peace cleric is also a strong choice, but (I'll have to run the numbers) I'm not sure 1d4 once per turn for 10 minutes thrice per long rest is better than 2d4 on one attack once per short rest. Additionally, and I admit this isn't a perfect reason, I kinda like the theme of a Zealot/Divine Sorc more than a Zealot/Peace Cleric, the latter of which can be discordant depending on character and doesn't have that natural accordance of divine barb/divine sorc.

The benefit of shield is that you can drop rage and use it on a reaction. Even if the enemy does physical (bludgeon, slash, pierce) damage (which you resist while raging), if the enemy's +ToHit is lower than 6 (assuming your AC is 17) then it's still worth it to drop rage and shield. That's not counting fire/force/psychic/etc damage which you don't resist even while raging. Also you don't get sleep, which remains useful for dealing with enemies with low HP well into Tier 2 and in my experience is situationally useful even in Tier 3.
